description: [NON-TERMINAL: Flow continues after this action] Retrieve the full invocation schema for a process. Call this AFTER discovery to get the JSON schema needed to construct valid action arguments. This is Step 2 of the two-step discovery workflow: (1) query_process_registry, (2) get_process_schema.
embedding_description: Fetch the full JSON schema for a specific process key. Get tool invocation arguments schema. Look up required and optional parameters for a discovered tool. Schema lookup for a process. Validate tool call arguments.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Schema result with action_status and data wrapper. data contains: process_key (the process identifier), description (what the process does), invocation_schema (full JSON Schema defining required and optional parameters), is_long_running (boolean indicating if user should be notified before invocation)
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Use invocation_schema to construct valid arguments when invoking a tool, or to explain parameters/usage when answering questions. Copy provider_type/provider/function_name exactly from schema const values. For outbound communication, resolve the active IO plugin namespace with query_process_registry, then invoke plugin::<namespace>::post_message with message and any namespace-specific arguments from its schema.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Retrieves the full JSON Schema for a process from the registry
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: NotFoundError: Process key does not exist in the registry. ValidationError: Invalid process key format (should be 'type::provider::function').
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For not found: The process may have been unregistered. Run query_process_registry again. For validation: Check the process_key format matches 'provider_type::provider::function_name'.
